prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1164; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound in the left-turn lane at an intersection in League City, Texas, when the collision occurred. While completing a left turn, Driver 1's vehicle was struck by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight through the intersection. Driver 1 identified themselves as the registered owner and the driver named on the policy covering the vehicle. A Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat, and both the Passenger and the officer confirmed the Passenger's presence in the vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated at the scene. The injury description is consistent with the type and force of the impact observed. Driver 2 stated that the collision happened as Driver 1 described, and two independent witnesses gave accounts that match. Scene photographs also show damage consistent with the reported sequence. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to Driver 1 or noted on inspection. It is not clear from the scene whether all of the visible damage resulted from this single impact, and this has been noted for further review.
